inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 339.395m common shares on the Q3-2026 10-Q cover at 2 Nov 2026 (already includes the 5.0m shares issued to the Cogentrix seller on 30 Oct 2026) plus 2.44m dilutive award shares (Q3-2026 diluted weighted average 337.853m less basic 335.413m). Held flat: SBC and award-tax withholding are expensed in the flows, and the buyback is the cash mechanism that keeps the count flat.
inputs.net_debt_basis: PRO FORMA for October-November 2026 events, because the forward flows include Cogentrix. 30 Sep 2026 balance sheet: long-term debt incl. current 21,146 + forward repurchase obligation (Nuveen Vistra Vision units) 622 - cash 2,743 = 19,025. Add: Cogentrix cash consideration 2,200 and assumed Cogentrix debt 1,700 (repaid 5 Nov from cash and Receivables/Repurchase facility draws), and 1,000 cash used to redeem Series A preferred on 15 Oct = 23,925. The NET figure is built from disclosed flows; the gross split (24,925 debt / 1,000 cash) is an estimate because the post-close facility draws are not itemised. Not included: proceeds from the Casco Bay/Beaver Falls/Syracuse sale closed 8 Oct (undisclosed; held-for-sale net assets 94), Q4 operating cash flow, Q4 buybacks. Restricted cash 33 and the 438 affiliate margin-deposit financing (matched by a 438 asset) excluded.
inputs.fcf_basis: TTM to 30 Sep 2026: OCF 5,762 (FY25 4,070 + 9M26 4,330 - 9M25 2,638) less capex incl. nuclear fuel and LTSA prepayments 3,155 (2,752 + 2,319 - 1,916). FY2025 as reported: FCF 1,318, owner FCF 1,154. Reported FCF is before growth capex being stripped, i.e. it is after ALL capex, unlike the company's 'Adjusted FCF before Growth'.
inputs.sbc_source: Cash-flow statement 'Stock-based compensation expense' TTM 127 (FY25 113 + 9M26 96 - 9M25 82) plus financing-activity 'Tax withholding on stock-based compensation' TTM ~73 (9M26 73; 9M25 51 and FY25 ~51). Two lines summed because Vistra publishes no combined figure; its Adjusted EBITDA adds back non-cash compensation, so the engine's SBC deduction is not a double charge.
inputs.buyback_note: TTM to 30 Sep 2026 financing-activity stock repurchases (FY25 1,028 + 9M26 917 - 9M25 776). Funded repurchaser: buybacks run ~6x the SBC charge, so the flat count is paid for; the share count has fallen from 482m (FY2021) to 340m.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD-built rate. Risk-free ~4.3% (10y UST), ERP ~5%, levered beta ~1.15 for a merchant generator/retailer -> cost of equity ~10%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~5.6% (BBB- senior notes issued 2026 at 4.55-5.55%, junior subordinated 7.0-7.25%), ~4.3% after tax. Market weights ~64% equity / 36% net debt and preferred -> ~8.0%; rounded UP to 8.5% for merchant commodity exposure. ONE rate for all three scenarios: the Texas data-centre interconnection risk, PJM market-design risk and commodity cyclicality are charged in the bear flows and the bear weight, not stacked into the discount rate (adaptations rule f).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment B (leases as operating cost). Total lease liabilities ~327 (FY2025), almost all US-GAAP operating leases whose cost is already inside Adjusted EBITDA; lease liabilities are excluded from net debt. Immaterial either way (<1% of EV).
inputs.nci_treatment: No deduction. NCI is 157 at 30 Sep 2026: a 35% third-party interest in a development JV formed Sept 2026 whose ~400 of assets are prepaid development spend not in the modelled flows. The former Vistra Vision minority (Nuveen/Avenue) was bought out in Dec 2024; the remaining deferred payment is the 622 forward repurchase obligation, carried in net debt.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, scenario-weighted (dcf-methods routing row 'operating company, cyclical' -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md). Vistra is an integrated merchant generator and retail electricity supplier, not a regulated utility, REIT or financial, so unlevered owner FCF at WACC less net debt is the right frame; first valuation of this ticker, no prior model. FY0 IS FY2026E, NOT FY2025: the net-debt anchor is pro forma to November 2026, so year 1 of the flows is FY2027; starting the flows at FY2026 would count ~10 months of already-spent 2026 cash flow twice (~USD 9/share). base_revenue 21,100 = 9M-2026 actual 16,004 + Q4 estimate ~5,100 (Q4-2025 4,584 plus two months of Cogentrix and higher capacity revenue). Revenue is a SCALER here, not the judgment: GAAP revenue includes unrealised hedge mark-to-market (9M-2026 +810), so the driver that carries the view is Ongoing Operations Adjusted EBITDA dollars (revenue x margin), anchored to guidance: FY2026 7.1-7.5bn, FY2027 7.7-8.5bn with management pointing toward the low end. EBITDA DEFINITION: Vistra's Adjusted EBITDA adds back nuclear fuel amortisation (D&A in the reconciliation is 2,473 for FY2025 vs 1,986 on the income statement), so D&A% uses the larger figure and capex% includes nuclear fuel purchases - consistent. It also excludes the Asset Closure segment, whose obligations are deducted in the equity bridge instead. CAPEX: 9M-2026 total 2,319 of which 1,503 is maintenance + nuclear fuel (sustaining ~2.0bn/yr pre-Cogentrix, ~2.2bn with it); the terminal capex of 10% of revenue (~2.9bn in FY2036 base) is sustaining spend inflated plus replacement capital, not today's growth programme. CASH TAX: ~nil federal for the next 12 months (management: ~4 federal, ~98 state; no CAMT), sheltered by bonus depreciation and the Cogentrix basis; ramped to 23% (21% federal + state) by FY2031 - the shelter is not perpetuated. WORKING CAPITAL: negative capture (-8% of revenue change) because retail receivables + fuel/materials inventory exceed payables (~2.2bn net on ~20.6bn TTM revenue). Interest income (17 for 9M-2026) not stripped: the company is in net debt. Preferred stock: Series A (1,000) redeemed 15 Oct 2026 and Series B (1,000) called for 15 Dec 2026, both funded by the Sept 2026 junior subordinated notes already in debt; Series B and C are deducted in the bridge at liquidation preference. Nuclear decommissioning AROs (3,497) are funded by the nuclear decommissioning trusts (inside 5,266 of investments; Comanche Peak trust 2,688 vs ARO 1,885 with the excess owed to Oncor) - both sides excluded. Helix Fund commitment (500 callable, 500 contingent) is an asset purchase at cost - excluded both sides. Price is a regular-session close, not an after-hours print.

equity_bridge.item: Preferred stock outstanding after Series A redemption (Series B 1,000 called for 15 Dec 2026; Series C 476)
equity_bridge.note: Q3-2026 10-Q note on preferred stock; liquidation preference USD 1,000/share

equity_bridge.item: Non-nuclear asset retirement obligations (lignite mine reclamation, coal ash, plant disposal), after tax at 23%
equity_bridge.note: Q3-2026 10-Q ARO note: 800 at 30 Sep 2026, unfunded; settled through the Asset Closure segment, which Ongoing Operations Adjusted EBITDA excludes

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_3yr_cagr, overridden in FY2027 by guidance and the Cogentrix full-year contribution
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR is not usable as the growth anchor: book equity fell from 8,361 (FY2020) to 5,110 (FY2025) because ~6.0bn of buybacks and the 2021-22 Winter Storm Uri and hedge mark-to-market losses ran through it, while Adjusted EBITDA nearly doubled (2,994 FY2022 -> 5,838 FY2025) largely through acquisitions (Energy Harbor, Lotus). Equity CAGR diverges from revenue and EPS by far more than 30%.
historical_growth.notes: FY2025 vs FY2022 (3yr) and FY2020 (5yr). EPS and owner-FCF 3yr CAGRs are undefined: FY2022 EPS was -3.26 and FY2022 owner FCF was -881 (reported -816 less SBC 65). Owner FCF 5yr: FY2020 2,013 (2,078 - 65) to FY2025 1,154 (1,318 - 113 - ~51 award taxes); the decline is growth capex (total capex 1,259 -> 2,752) and the FY2025 Moss Landing/Martin Lake outage year, not deterioration in the base business. Equity-award tax withholding is only disclosed from 2024, so earlier owner-FCF years deduct the SBC add-back alone. SBC is small (under 1% of revenue) so reported and owner FCF CAGRs are close.

base.rationale: FY2027 Adjusted EBITDA ~8.0bn (23,210 x 34.5%), just below the 8.1bn guidance midpoint because management itself points to the low end. Growth to ~8.9bn by FY2031 from the AWS and Meta nuclear PPA ramps, PJM capacity at ~USD 325-333/MW-day and Cogentrix; margin then fades 34.5% -> 33% as merchant spreads normalise and coal units retire, giving ~9.7bn in FY2036. Cap multiple 14x (cyclical band 12-15x) binds against a 17x Gordon value.

bull.rationale: FY2027 Adjusted EBITDA ~8.4bn (upper half of guidance), compounding to ~12.5bn by FY2036 as more of the fleet is contracted at a premium and ERCOT prices rise from ~USD 30/MWh. Higher capex throughout (uprates, new gas builds) is the price of that growth. Cap 16x, one turn above the cyclical band, because a largely contracted nuclear and gas fleet is a less cyclical asset.

bear.rationale: FY2027 Adjusted EBITDA ~7.6bn, just under the low end of guidance (the book is substantially hedged, so 2027 cannot fall far). As hedges roll off into weaker markets EBITDA falls to ~6.1bn by FY2030 and recovers only with inflation to ~6.6bn by FY2036. Growth capex is cut to sustaining levels. Cap 12x, the bottom of the cyclical band.

scenario_narratives.base: Guidance holds and the contracted layer builds, but the merchant fleet earns no more than it does today. FY2027 lands near the low-to-mid part of the 7.7-8.5bn range with a full year of Cogentrix. The 20-year AWS (1,200 MW, Comanche Peak) and Meta (2,609 MW, PJM nuclear) contracts ramp through the early 2030s and PJM capacity keeps clearing near the cap, lifting Adjusted EBITDA toward 9bn by FY2031. Texas adopts large-load rules that slow, but do not stop, data-centre interconnection, so ERCOT pricing stays near today's subdued level rather than tightening. From FY2031 the margin fades as coal units retire or repower and merchant spreads normalise. Growth capex (uprates, Permian peakers, coal-to-gas repowering) tapers to sustaining spend, and the federal cash-tax shelter is used up by FY2031.
scenario_narratives.bull: The data-centre load is real and Vistra's existing plants are the fastest way to serve it. Management's 12-15 GW 'realistic' 2030 queue arrives, the Texas interconnection pause is watered down in the legislature, and ERCOT prices rise from ~USD 30/MWh toward new-build cost. Further long-term contracts are signed on the gas and remaining nuclear fleet at premiums to forward curves, the 433 MW of nuclear uprates deliver, PJM capacity stays at or near the cap beyond 2028-29, and the 45U nuclear credit guidance lands favourably. Adjusted EBITDA reaches the upper half of FY2027 guidance and compounds to ~12.5bn by FY2036, with a rising contracted share justifying a higher exit multiple.
scenario_narratives.bear: The AI power trade unwinds and Texas turns hostile. The governor-elect's pause on new data-centre grid connections becomes policy, Senate Bill 6 curtailment rules bite, and the Q3-2026 wave of data-centre cancellations continues, leaving ERCOT (46% of capacity) oversupplied as renewables and batteries keep arriving and market heat rates compress. PJM lowers its capacity price cap or runs a reliability backstop auction that undercuts the USD 325/MW-day print, low natural gas prices pull power prices down, and Treasury's 45U 'gross receipts' definition cuts recognised nuclear credits. The hedge book protects FY2027; after it rolls off, Adjusted EBITDA falls to ~6bn, close to the FY2025 level despite two acquisitions. With ~24bn of net debt and 1.5bn of preferred ahead of the equity, a 25% fall in EBITDA takes roughly two thirds off the equity value: leverage, not solvency, is what makes this case severe.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the house default 15/50/35 to 25/50/25. Bear raised to 25%: a single political jurisdiction (Texas, 46% of capacity and the largest retail base) has a governor-elect pledged to pause data-centre interconnections, most of the fleet is still merchant, and ~24bn of net debt gears any EBITDA shortfall roughly threefold into the equity. Base held at 50%: FY2026 guidance was raised and narrowed, FY2027 is substantially hedged and the two nuclear contracts are signed with investment-grade counterparties. Bull cut to 25%: it needs several independent things to go right at once - data-centre load arriving, Texas policy softening, PJM capacity prices holding and more contracts at premium prices - while management's own demand estimate is a small fraction of headline queues.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Vistra is valued as a geared, cyclical cash generator whose earnings base stepped up through acquisitions and long-term nuclear contracts, not as a growth compounder. The judgment is carried by Adjusted EBITDA dollars against guidance, converted to owner FCF after ALL capex (including growth capex and nuclear fuel), award costs and a cash-tax rate that normalises to 23%. Risk is charged once, in the scenario flows and weights, at a single 8.5% WACC. The terminal value is capped at 12-16x owner FCF, which binds in all three scenarios and equates to roughly 6-8x terminal EBITDA.
key_risks_to_valuation: Leverage: ~24bn of pro forma net debt plus 1.5bn of preferred means each 1bn of sustainable EBITDA is worth roughly USD 20-25 per share; the bear-to-bull range is wide for that reason
The net-debt anchor is pro forma for October-November 2026 (Cogentrix, Series A redemption) and built from disclosed flows, not from a published balance sheet; the FY2026 10-K will replace it
Texas policy: a pause on data-centre interconnection and SB6 curtailment rules decide whether ERCOT tightens or stays oversupplied
Mid-cycle uncertainty: PJM capacity prices are at the administrative cap; the base case assumes they hold near it and that merchant margins fade only modestly
Cash-tax shelter: federal cash taxes are ~nil today; a faster or slower ramp to 23% moves value by several dollars per share
45U nuclear production tax credit: Treasury has not finalised the gross-receipts definition (220 recognised in FY2025)
Terminal capex: sustaining spend of ~10% of revenue is a judgment on an ageing fleet with ~20% coal; a higher replacement burden lowers every scenario
base_revenue and FY2026 EBITDA are estimates with one quarter still unreported
